title: HTTP and Networking Fundamentals
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of http and networking fundamentals in a C#/.NET program.
Predict the result of the included C# example and verify the documented output.
Apply http and networking fundamentals to a small task and identify one relevant boundary, limitation, or version requirement.

content.intro: HTTP and Networking Fundamentals is lesson 150 in APIs, Networking, and Database Integration. Integration code should isolate network or database calls, use parameters instead of string-built commands, validate external data, and define transaction boundaries.
content.why_it_matters: External systems fail and return untrusted data, so integration code needs timeouts, validation, and clear data boundaries. This lesson focuses on http and networking fundamentals and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Integration code should isolate network or database calls, use parameters instead of string-built commands, validate external data, and define transaction boundaries.

content_blocks.title: A practical way to learn it
content_blocks.text: Start with the smallest valid case for http and networking fundamentals. Predict the output, run or inspect the example in the stated toolchain, then change one input or rule and compare the result. For production code, record assumptions and verify boundary cases.

items.title: Requests and responses
items.text: For requests and responses, define the expected behavior, inspect how it relates to http and networking fundamentals, and verify a representative case plus one boundary or failure case.

items.title: HTTP methods
items.text: Use explicit timeouts, parameterized database commands, small service boundaries, and validation for external results.

items.title: Status codes
items.text: Treat HTTP and database responses as untrusted boundaries. Set timeouts, check status codes, parameterize SQL, validate deserialized results, and make transaction scope and disposal explicit.

items.title: Headers and content types
items.text: Treat HTTP and database responses as untrusted boundaries. Set timeouts, check status codes, parameterize SQL, validate deserialized results, and make transaction scope and disposal explicit.

items.title: JSON-based communication
items.text: Validate serialized input and version its schema where needed; successful parsing does not guarantee valid business data.

items.title: Network failures and timeouts
items.text: Await I/O-bound tasks, pass cancellation tokens across boundaries, and protect shared mutable state explicitly.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small C# example that demonstrates http and networking fundamentals. Change one input or implementation detail, predict the result, then check it locally and explain one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates http and networking fundamentals rather than only repeating its definition.
The result is checked locally or against a clearly documented reference output.
At least one relevant boundary, invalid-input case, or compatibility condition is considered.
hints: List the assumptions and expected behavior for http and networking fundamentals before editing the code.
Change one variable or rule at a time; keep the previous output for comparison.
If behavior differs, confirm the compiler/target framework and consult the linked official documentation.
content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: identify the expected input and output, start from the smallest example, use the feature only where it clarifies the rule, and verify both a typical case and a boundary/failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the feature works identically on every target
common_mistakes.why: Language syntax, libraries, and runtime support are version-dependent.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the target framework and official versioned reference before using the feature.

common_mistakes.why: Boundary values, malformed input, and failure states often expose the real bug.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one typical input and one boundary or invalid case to the manual or automated checks.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating sample output as proof that the code ran
common_mistakes.why: The course reader uses static reference output for C# because it has no C# execution runner.
common_mistakes.fix: Run the snippet in a local .NET project or a separately isolated execution service.
